short_description.id: Tamayorihime adalah dewi dalam mitologi Jepang, putri dewa laut yang dalam kisah Jinmu menjadi ibu Kaisar Jinmu.
short_description.en: Tamayorihime is a goddess of Japanese mythology, a sea god's daughter who in the Jinmu line is the mother of Emperor Jinmu.

long_description.id: Tamayorihime adalah dewi dalam mitologi Jepang. Kojiki menulis namanya 玉依毘売命 dan Nihon Shoki menulis 玉依姫. Ia putri dewa laut Watatsumi dan adik Toyotamahime.
long_description.en: Tamayorihime is a goddess in Japanese mythology. The Kojiki spells her name 玉依毘売命 and the Nihon Shoki 玉依姫. She is the daughter of the sea god Watatsumi and has Toyotamahime as her elder sister.

long_description.id: Ketika Toyotamahime meninggalkan suaminya Hoori, ia mengirim Tamayorihime untuk merawat putra mereka, Ugayafukiaezu. Dalam versi Nihon Shoki, Tamayorihime justru menemani kakaknya ke dunia manusia saat hendak melahirkan. Kamus Jepang menyebut bahwa ia kemudian menikahi anak itu dan melahirkan empat putra, termasuk Kamuyamato-Iwarebiko (Kaisar Jinmu).
long_description.en: After Toyotamahime left her husband Hoori, she sent Tamayorihime to look after their son Ugayafukiaezu; in the Nihon Shoki version, however, Tamayorihime goes with her sister to the human world as the birth approaches. A Japanese dictionary says she later married the child and bore four sons, including Kamuyamato-Iwarebiko (Emperor Jinmu).

long_description.id: Nama Tamayorihime juga dipakai untuk perempuan lain dalam tradisi Jepang, misalnya dalam legenda Kamo dan dalam kisah ibu leluhur klan Miwa. Ensiklopedia Heibonsha menilai nama itu lebih tepat dipahami sebagai kata benda umum untuk perempuan yang dirasuki roh ilahi, dan kamus menjelaskan bahwa 'tama' berarti jiwa dan 'yori' berarti merasuk.
long_description.en: The name Tamayorihime is also given to other women in Japanese tradition, for example in the Kamo legend and in the story of the mother of the Miwa ancestor. The Heibonsha encyclopedia holds that the name is better understood as a common noun for a woman on whom a divine spirit descends, and a dictionary explains that 'tama' means soul and 'yori' means to possess.

long_description.id: Kuil Miyaura di Nichinan, Prefektur Miyazaki, dipercaya sebagai tempat kediamannya.
long_description.en: Miyaura Shrine in Nichinan City, Miyazaki Prefecture, is said to be the site of her residence.

cultural_context.id: Kata tamayori-hime merupakan istilah umum bagi pendeta perempuan yang mengabdikan hidup kepada dewa mereka, dan Ensiklopedia Heibonsha menilai semua miko kuno dapat disebut Tamayorihime.
cultural_context.en: Tamayori-hime serves as a general term for female shamans devoted entirely to their deities, and the Heibonsha encyclopedia holds that all ancient miko can be called Tamayorihime.

literal_meaning.id: "tama" berarti jiwa, "yori" berarti merasuk; perempuan yang dirasuki roh ilahi
literal_meaning.en: "tama" means soul and "yori" means to possess; a woman on whom a divine spirit descends

who.id: Tamayorihime adalah dewi dalam mitologi Jepang, putri dewa laut Watatsumi.
who.en: Tamayorihime is a goddess in Japanese mythology, a daughter of the sea-dragon god Watatsumi.

origin.id: Ia putri dewa laut dan adik Toyotamahime menurut Kojiki dan Nihon Shoki.
origin.en: She is a sea god's daughter and the younger sister of Toyotamahime in the Kojiki and Nihon Shoki.

role.id: Ia merawat putra Toyotamahime lalu, menurut kamus, menjadi istrinya.
role.en: She cares for Toyotamahime's son and, according to the dictionary, later becomes his wife.

famous_for.id: Ia dikenal sebagai ibu Kaisar Jinmu menurut kamus Jepang.
famous_for.en: She is known as the mother of Emperor Jinmu according to the Japanese dictionary.

did_you_know.id: Ensiklopedia Heibonsha menilai nama Tamayorihime lebih cocok sebagai kata benda umum untuk perempuan yang dirasuki roh ilahi daripada nama diri.
did_you_know.en: The Heibonsha encyclopedia holds that Tamayorihime is better understood as a common noun for a woman possessed by a divine spirit than as a proper name.

description.id: Dalam legenda Kamo, ia putri Taketsunumi, menikah dengan anak panah bercat merah (Hoikazuchi), dan melahirkan Wakeikazuchi.
description.en: In the Kamo legend she is a daughter of Taketsunumi, marries a red-painted arrow (Hoikazuchi), and bears Wakeikazuchi.

role.id: Tamayorihime membesarkan anak kakaknya.
role.en: Tamayorihime raises her sister's child.

summary.id: Setelah Toyotamahime melahirkan putra Hoori dan pergi, Tamayorihime merawat anak itu. Nihon Shoki menambahkan versi bahwa ia menemani kakaknya ke dunia manusia saat hendak melahirkan.
summary.en: After Toyotamahime bore Hoori's son and left, Tamayorihime looked after the child. The Nihon Shoki adds a version in which she goes with her sister to the human world as the birth approaches.

description.id: Dipercaya sebagai tempat kediaman Tamayorihime.
description.en: Said to be the site of Tamayorihime's residence.

note.id: Tamayorihime putri dewa laut Watatsumi.
note.en: Tamayorihime is the daughter of the sea god Watatsumi.

note.id: Toyotamahime adalah kakaknya; satu pandangan menilai keduanya aspek satu dewi.
note.en: Toyotamahime is her elder sister; one view treats the two as aspects of one goddess.

note.id: Ia dirawat Tamayorihime dan kemudian, menurut kamus, menjadi suaminya.
note.en: He was raised by Tamayorihime and later, according to the dictionary, became her husband.

learning_questions.id: Mengapa satu nama dewi dapat dipakai untuk beberapa perempuan dalam tradisi yang berbeda?
learning_questions.en: Why can one goddess name be used for several women in different traditions?

learning_questions.id: Apa akibatnya bila sebuah nama dipahami sebagai gelar, bukan nama diri?
learning_questions.en: What changes when a name is understood as a title rather than a proper name?

sources.title: 玉依姫とは (コトバンク)
sources.publisher: コトバンク (デジタル大辞泉, 精選版 日本国語大辞典, 改訂新版 世界大百科事典)

claims.quote: Tamayori-hime is a goddess in Japanese mythology.

statement.id: Tamayori - hime adalah dewi dalam mitologi Jepang.
statement.en: Tamayori-hime is a goddess in Japanese mythology.

claims.quote: Her name is spelled as 玉依毘売命 in the Kojiki and 玉依姫 in the Nihon Shoki.

statement.id: Kojiki dan Nihon Shoki menuliskan namanya secara berbeda.
statement.en: The Kojiki and Nihon Shoki write her name differently.

claims.quote: Tamayori-hime is the daughter of the sea-dragon god Watatsumi and the younger sister of Toyotama-hime.

statement.id: Dia digambarkan sebagai putri Watatsumi dan saudara perempuan Toyotama - hime.
statement.en: She is described as a daughter of Watatsumi and sister of Toyotama-hime.

claims.quote: When Toyotama-hime abandoned her husband Hoori, she sent Tamayori-hime to care for their son Ugayafukiaezu, although in the Nihon Shoki version of the legend, Tamayori-hime accompanies her sister to the human world when she was about to give birth.

statement.id: Satu akun mengatakan dia merawat putra Toyotama - hime.
statement.en: One account says she cared for Toyotama-hime’s son.

claims.quote: 日本神話で、海の神の娘。 鸕鷀草葺不合尊 うがやふきあえずのみこと の妃となり、 神日本磐余彦尊 かんやまといわれびこのみこと （神武天皇）ら四子を産んだ。

statement.id: Menurut Digital Daijisen, dalam mitologi Jepang ia putri dewa laut, menjadi permaisuri Ugayafukiaezu dan melahirkan empat putra, termasuk Kamuyamato-Iwarebiko (Kaisar Jinmu).
statement.en: According to the Digital Daijisen, in Japanese mythology she is a daughter of a sea god who became the consort of Ugayafukiaezu and bore four sons, including Kamuyamato-Iwarebiko (Emperor Jinmu).

claims.quote: 賀茂伝説で、 建角身命 たけつぬみのみこと の娘。 丹塗矢 にぬりや （ 火雷神 ほのいかずちのかみ ）と結婚し、 別雷神 わけいかずちのかみ を産んだ。

statement.id: Dalam legenda Kamo, ia putri Taketsunumi; ia menikah dengan anak panah bercat merah (Hoikazuchi) dan melahirkan Wakeikazuchi.
statement.en: In the Kamo legend she is a daughter of Taketsunumi; she marries a red-painted arrow (Hoikazuchi) and bears Wakeikazuchi.

claims.quote: 姉の豊玉姫が天孫彦火火出見尊(ひこほほでみのみこと)の子彦波瀲武鸕鷀草葺不合尊(ひこなぎさたけうがやふきあえずのみこと)を産み落として去った後、其の子を養育した。
claims.locator: 精選版 日本国語大辞典

statement.id: Setelah kakaknya, Toyotamahime, melahirkan putra Hikonagisatake-Ugayafukiaezu dan pergi, Tamayorihime membesarkan anak itu.
statement.en: After her elder sister Toyotamahime bore the child Hikonagisatake-Ugayafukiaezu and left, Tamayorihime raised that child.

claims.quote: ( 古く「たまよりびめ」とも。「たま」は魂、「より」は憑依する意 )
claims.locator: 精選版 日本国語大辞典

statement.id: Kamus ini menjelaskan bahwa "tama" berarti roh/jiwa dan "yori" berarti merasuk (mengambil alih).
statement.en: The dictionary explains that "tama" means soul and "yori" means to possess.

claims.quote: 物語の中では固有名詞のように扱われているが，むしろ普通名詞と考えたほうがよい。タマヨリヒメとは神霊が依り憑（つ）く女性の意である。
claims.locator: 改訂新版 世界大百科事典

statement.id: Ensiklopedia Heibonsha menilai bahwa meskipun dalam kisah diperlakukan seperti nama diri, Tamayorihime lebih baik dianggap kata benda umum yang berarti perempuan yang dirasuki roh ilahi.
statement.en: The Heibonsha encyclopedia holds that although treated like a proper name in the stories, Tamayorihime is better regarded as a common noun meaning a woman on whom a divine spirit descends.

claims.quote: これは，祭儀の際，神降臨の秘儀に立ち会う巫女が，神話的には神に感精してその子を生む母として形象化されたものである。古代の巫女はなべてタマヨリヒメであったといえる。
claims.locator: 改訂新版 世界大百科事典

statement.id: Menurut ensiklopedia itu, miko yang menyaksikan turunnya dewa dalam upacara digambarkan dalam mitos sebagai ibu yang mengandung anak dewa, dan semua miko kuno dapat disebut Tamayorihime.
statement.en: According to the encyclopedia, the miko who attended the descent of a god during rites is imagined in myth as a mother who conceives the god's child, and all ancient miko can be called Tamayorihime.

claims.quote: 記紀，《風土記》に登場する女性の名。たとえば，毎夜訪れる見知らぬ若者（実は大物主（おおものぬし）神）によってみごもり，三輪氏の祖を生んだとされる女性，海神（わたつみ）の娘で，海幸山幸神話の主人公火遠理（ほおり）命の子の乳母でのちには妻となり，神武天皇を生んだとされる女性，丹塗矢（にぬりや）と化した火雷（ほのいかずち）神に感精して賀茂氏の祖神を生んだとされる女性などがタマヨリヒメとよばれている。
claims.locator: 改訂新版 世界大百科事典

statement.id: Beberapa perempuan dalam Kiki dan Fudoki disebut Tamayorihime: ibu leluhur klan Miwa yang dikunjungi pemuda misterius (Ōmononushi), putri dewa laut yang kemudian menjadi istri dan melahirkan Kaisar Jinmu, dan perempuan yang melahirkan leluhur klan Kamo setelah dibuahi Hoikazuchi yang menjelma anak panah.
statement.en: Several women in the Kiki and the Fudoki are called Tamayorihime: the mother of the Miwa ancestor who was visited by a mysterious youth (Ōmononushi), the sea god's daughter who nursed and later married and bore Emperor Jinmu, and the woman who bore the Kamo ancestor after Hoikazuchi, in the form of a red arrow, impregnated her.

claims.quote: Toshio Akima of the International Research Centre for Japanese Studies considers it more likely that Tamayori-hime is not the sister of Toyotama-hime, but that the two should be considered as aspects of the same, single deity.

statement.id: Toshio Akima menilai lebih mungkin Tamayori-hime bukan adik Toyotama-hime, melainkan keduanya aspek dari satu dewi.
statement.en: Toshio Akima considers it more likely that Tamayori-hime is not the sister of Toyotama-hime but that the two are aspects of a single deity.

claims.quote: The word tamayori-hime is a generic term for shamanesses who dedicated their lives exclusively to their deities.

statement.id: Kata tamayori-hime merupakan istilah umum bagi pendeta perempuan (shamaness) yang mengabdikan hidup kepada dewa mereka.
statement.en: The word tamayori-hime is a generic term for shamanesses who dedicated their lives exclusively to their deities.

claims.quote: Miyaura Shrine (Miyazaki Prefecture Nichinan City) is said to be the site of Tamayorihime's residence.

statement.id: Kuil Miyaura di Nichinan, Prefektur Miyazaki, dipercaya sebagai tempat kediaman Tamayorihime.
statement.en: Miyaura Shrine in Nichinan City, Miyazaki Prefecture, is said to be the site of Tamayorihime's residence.

summary.id: Kojiki dan Nihon Shoki: ia adik Toyotamahime.
summary.en: The Kojiki and Nihon Shoki: she is the younger sister of Toyotamahime.

summary.id: Toshio Akima: lebih mungkin keduanya aspek satu dewi yang sama.
summary.en: Toshio Akima: more likely the two are aspects of the same single deity.

items.reason: Klaim kini menyebut dewi/perempuan pengasuh dan ibu dalam beberapa tradisi, tanpa rupa khusus atau kuasa visual aktif. Putri Watatsumi tidak mengizinkan ekor naga, ombak yang diperintah atau skala kosmis rekaan; anak panah merah adalah Hoikazuchi dalam varian Kamo, bukan atribut pengendalian petir miliknya. Sosok perempuan berpakaian saja berisiko manusia biasa.

short_description.id: Tardo adalah duende jahat dari cerita rakyat Galisia dan Portugal yang masuk ke rumah pada malam hari dan duduk di dada orang tidur, menimbulkan mimpi buruk.
short_description.en: The tardo is a malevolent duende of Galician and Portuguese folklore that enters houses at night and sits on sleepers' chests, causing nightmares.

long_description.id: Tardo adalah duende mitologi Galisia, mirip trasno tetapi jauh lebih jahat; dalam cerita rakyat Portugal ia juga disebut pesadelo. Ia kecil, berbulu, bergigi banyak, kehijauan, berjanggut, bertopi merah, dan membawa pedang kecil. Ia tinggal di bawah tanah dan pada malam hari masuk ke rumah untuk duduk di dada orang tidur, menimbulkan sakit dan mimpi buruk.
long_description.en: The tardo is a duende of Galician mythology, like the trasno but far nastier; in Portuguese folklore it is also called pesadelo. It is small, hairy, many-toothed, greenish, bearded, red-capped and carries a small sword. It lives underground and at night gets into houses to sit on sleepers' chests, causing pain and nightmares.

long_description.id: Ia bisa berwujud anjing, kucing, atau kambing, dan di persimpangan membuat orang tersesat dengan mengencingi kaki mereka. Untuk mengusirnya orang menaruh mangkuk biji-bijian, karena tardo akan terus menghitungnya sampai pagi.
long_description.en: It can take the form of a dog, cat or goat, and at crossroads makes people lose their way by urinating on their legs. To be rid of it people leave a bowl of grain, which the tardo will keep counting until morning.

who.id: Duende jahat penindih dada.
who.en: A malevolent chest-sitting duende.

origin.en: Galicia and Portugal.

role.id: Menimbulkan mimpi buruk.
role.en: Causes nightmares.

description.id: Tardo hanya bisa menghitung sampai seratus sehingga sibuk menghitung biji sampai pagi.
description.en: The tardo can only count to a hundred, so it counts the grains until dawn.

note.id: Duende Galisia yang mirip tetapi tidak sejahat tardo.
note.en: A similar but less malevolent Galician duende.

description.id: Seorang tokoh mengaku memelihara tardo jinak.
description.en: A character claims to keep a tame tardo.

claims.quote: El tardo es un duende de la mitología gallega, similar al trasno pero mucho más malévolo.

statement.id: Tardo adalah duende (peri rumah) mitologi Galisia, mirip trasno tetapi jauh lebih jahat.
statement.en: The tardo is a duende (house sprite) of Galician mythology, like the trasno but far more malevolent.

claims.quote: Es pequeño, peludo, con muchos dientes, de color verdoso y ojos redondos y negros; tiene barba y va vestido con ropas viejas y un gorro rojo. Además, se diferencia de otros duendes porque lleva una pequeña y afilada espada.

statement.id: Ia kecil, berbulu, bergigi banyak, berwarna kehijauan dengan mata bulat hitam, berjanggut, berpakaian tua dan bertopi merah; berbeda dari duende lain, ia membawa pedang kecil yang tajam.
statement.en: It is small, hairy and many-toothed, greenish with round black eyes, bearded, in old clothes and a red cap; unlike other duendes it carries a small sharp sword.

claims.quote: Acostumbra a vivir bajo tierra y aprovecha la oscuridad de la noche para entrar en las casas, y así, sentarse sobre el pecho de las personas dormidas, provocándoles dolor y terribles pesadillas.

statement.id: Ia biasa tinggal di bawah tanah dan memanfaatkan gelap malam untuk masuk ke rumah lalu duduk di dada orang tidur, menimbulkan rasa sakit dan mimpi buruk.
statement.en: It usually lives underground and uses the dark of night to get into houses and sit on sleepers' chests, causing pain and terrible nightmares.

claims.quote: Para librarse de él basta con dejar un cuenco con granos de maíz o algún otro cereal. Como es muy curioso, irá a ver el cuenco y empezará a contar los granos, pero como sólo sabe contar hasta cien, volverá a empezar una y otra vez

statement.id: Untuk mengusirnya cukup menaruh mangkuk berisi biji jagung atau serealia lain; karena sangat ingin tahu, ia akan menghitung bijinya, tetapi hanya bisa menghitung sampai seratus sehingga terus mengulang dari awal.
statement.en: To be rid of it, simply leave a bowl of maize or other grain; being very curious it will count the grains, but since it can only count to a hundred it starts over and over.

claims.quote: O Tardo ou Trevor é uma espécie de duende, um ser mítico do folclore popular português e galego. Ao tardo também se chama pesadelo ou tardo moleiro.

statement.id: Menurut artikel bahasa Portugis, Tardo atau Trevor adalah sejenis duende dalam cerita rakyat Portugal dan Galisia, juga disebut pesadelo atau tardo moleiro.
statement.en: According to the Portuguese article, the Tardo or Trevor is a kind of duende of Portuguese and Galician folklore, also called pesadelo or tardo moleiro.

claims.quote: O tardo pode aparecer na figura de um animal e frequentemente aparece na figura de um cão, gato ou cabra.

statement.id: Tardo dapat muncul berwujud hewan, sering sebagai anjing, kucing, atau kambing.
statement.en: The tardo can appear as an animal, often a dog, cat or goat.

claims.quote: O tardo quando aparece nos caminhos, nos regatos e nas encruzilhadas tenta deixar as pessoas intardadas (desorientadas) sem saber qual caminho seguir, urinando nas pernas das pessoas.

statement.id: Di jalan, sungai kecil, dan persimpangan, tardo berusaha membuat orang tersesat dengan mengencingi kaki mereka.
statement.en: On roads, by streams and at crossroads the tardo tries to make people lose their way by urinating on their legs.

claims.quote: Eliseo Alonsoren A rúa do noxo eleberrian, protagonistetako batek dio, mozkortuta dagoenean, berarekin batera bezatutako tardo bat duela.

statement.id: Menurut artikel bahasa Basque, dalam novel Eliseo Alonso A rúa do noxo seorang tokoh utama yang mabuk mengaku memelihara tardo jinak.
statement.en: According to the Basque article, in Eliseo Alonso's novel A rúa do noxo a drunken protagonist claims to keep a tame tardo.

short_description.id: Te Wheke-a-Muturangi adalah monster gurita raksasa dalam mitologi Māori yang diburu melintasi samudra dan dibunuh oleh Kupe.
short_description.en: Te Wheke-a-Muturangi is a monstrous giant octopus in Māori mythology pursued and slain by Kupe the navigator.

long_description.id: Dalam mitologi Māori, Te Wheke-a-Muturangi adalah gurita raksasa yang menakutkan, hewan peliharaan atau familiar Muturangi, seorang tohunga sakti dari Hawaiki. Gurita itu tetap makhluk liar dan penjaga.
long_description.en: Te Wheke-a-Muturangi, from Māori mythology, is a monstrous octopus kept as a pet or familiar by Muturangi, a mighty tohunga from Hawaiki. Even so, it remained a wild animal and a guardian.

long_description.id: Menurut satu versi, ketika Kupe tiba di New Zealand ia bertemu makhluk itu di lepas Castlepoint. Gurita raksasa itu lari menyeberangi Cook Strait dan dikejar Kupe melalui Tory Channel. Di sana terjadi pertempuran besar, dan ketika gurita itu hendak melarikan diri, Kupe memotong lengannya dengan kapak adze sehingga membunuhnya.
long_description.en: One version tells that Kupe met the beast off Castlepoint on arriving in New Zealand. The giant octopus fled over Cook Strait with Kupe in pursuit through Tory Channel, where a great fight occurred; as the octopus seemed about to escape, Kupe hacked off its arms with his adze and killed it.

long_description.id: Dalam kumpulan Grey, makhluk yang lari dari Castle Point itu dinamai Kupe Te Wheke-a-Muturangi dan bersembunyi di arus Tory Channel. Ia mendengar kano Kupe mendekat dan mengangkat lengannya untuk menangkap dan melahap kano beserta awaknya. Kupe melemparkan labu besar ke laut; monster itu menyerangnya karena mengira itu kano, lalu Kupe menebasnya dengan kapak dan membelahnya menjadi dua hingga mati.
long_description.en: In Grey's collection, the creature that had fled from Castle Point was named by Kupe Te Wheke-a-Muturangi and lay hidden in the current of Tory Channel. It heard Kupe's canoe approaching and raised its arms to catch and devour the canoe and its crew. Kupe threw a large calabash overboard; the monster attacked it, thinking it was the canoe, and Kupe struck it with his axe and severed it in two, killing it.

who.id: Monster gurita raksasa peliharaan tohunga Muturangi dari Hawaiki.
who.en: A giant monstrous octopus belonging to tohunga Muturangi of Hawaiki.

origin.id: Legenda pelayaran penjelajahan samudra oleh Kupe ke New Zealand.
origin.en: Voyaging and discovery traditions of Kupe in New Zealand.

role.id: Monster samudra penghalang navigasi yang ditumpas oleh penjelajah Kupe.
role.en: Oceanic obstacle monster slain by navigator Kupe.

famous_for.id: Pertarungan epiknya melawan Kupe di Tory Channel yang berujung pemotongan tentakelnya.
famous_for.en: Epic battle against Kupe in Tory Channel resulting in its arms being severed.

did_you_know.id: Kupe memotong tentakel Te Wheke-a-Muturangi menggunakan beliung batu (adze) saat monster itu hendak melarikan diri di Tory Channel.
did_you_know.en: Kupe severed the arms of Te Wheke-a-Muturangi with his adze when the giant octopus attempted to flee through Tory Channel.

description.id: Dalam kumpulan Grey, monster itu menyerang labu besar yang dilemparkan Kupe karena mengira itu kano Kupe, sehingga Kupe dapat menebasnya.
description.en: In Grey's collection, the monster flew at the large calabash Kupe threw overboard, thinking it was Kupe's canoe, which let Kupe strike it down.

title.en: Kupe and the octopus of Muturangi

role.id: Monster yang dikejar dan akhirnya dibunuh Kupe.
role.en: The monster chased and finally slain by Kupe.

summary.id: Kupe mengejar gurita raksasa itu menyeberangi Cook Strait hingga Tory Channel; dalam satu versi ia memotong lengannya dengan kapak adze, dalam versi Grey ia memancingnya dengan labu besar lalu membelahnya dengan kapak.
summary.en: Kupe chases the giant octopus across Cook Strait to Tory Channel; in one version he cuts off its arms with his adze, in Grey's version he lures it with a large calabash and then severs it with his axe.

note.id: Kupe mengejar gurita raksasa itu hingga Tory Channel dan membunuhnya.
note.en: Kupe chased the giant octopus to Tory Channel and killed it.

learning_questions.en: How did the pursuit of Te Wheke-a-Muturangi by Kupe serve as a geographic naming map for coastal New Zealand?

statement.id: Te Wheke-a-Muturangi adalah monster gurita yang dibunuh di Tory Channel oleh penjelajah Kupe.
statement.en: Te Wheke-a-Muturangi is a monstrous octopus destroyed in Tory Channel by Kupe.

short_description.id: Tephras adalah iblis "roh abu" dalam Wasiat Salomo yang membakar ladang dan dipaksa Salomo mengangkat batu untuk pembangunan Bait Allah.
short_description.en: Tephras is the "spirit of ash" demon of the Testament of Solomon who burns fields and is forced by Solomon to lift stones for the Temple.

long_description.id: Tephras adalah iblis dalam mitologi Yahudi yang dijuluki "roh abu". Kepalanya tegak, tetapi tubuhnya melengkung seperti siput, dan ia selalu membawa badai debu. Ia digambarkan dalam Wasiat Salomo, teks apokrif Perjanjian Lama.
long_description.en: Tephras is a demon of Jewish mythology nicknamed the "spirit of ash". It holds its head high but its body is bent like a snail, and it always brings a dust storm. It is described in the Testament of Solomon, an Old Testament apocryphon.

long_description.id: Ketika dipanggil Salomo, Tephras mengaku membawa kegelapan, membakar ladang, dan merugikan pertanian, terutama pada musim panas, dan menyebut dirinya tunduk pada malaikat agung Azael. Salomo lalu menyegelnya dan memaksanya mengangkat batu untuk para pekerja Bait Allah.
long_description.en: Summoned by Solomon, Tephras confessed that it brings darkness, burns fields and harms farms, mostly in summer, and named the archangel Azael as its master. Solomon then sealed it and set it to lifting stones for the Temple workers.

long_description.id: Dalam terjemahan Wasiat Salomo, roh ini datang dengan wajah terangkat tinggi, sementara sisa tubuhnya melingkar seperti siput. Ia membawa kegelapan pada manusia, membakar ladang, menghancurkan rumah pertanian, paling sibuk pada musim panas, dan menyusup ke sudut-sudut tembok siang dan malam. Bintangnya berada di ujung tanduk bulan ketika bulan di selatan, dan ia mengaku bertugas menahan kejang demam hemitertian. Salomo memanggil malaikat agung Azael, menyegelnya, dan menyuruhnya melemparkan batu-batu besar kepada para pekerja di bagian atas Bait Suci.
long_description.en: In the translated Testament of Solomon this spirit arrives with its face carried high while the rest of it curls away like a snail. It brings darkness on men, sets fire to fields, ruins homesteads, is busiest in summer and creeps into corners of the wall by night and day. Its star is at the tip of the moon's horn when the moon is in the south, and it claims the task of restraining the convulsions of the hemitertian fever. Solomon summoned the archangel Azael, sealed it and made it toss great stones up to the workmen on the higher parts of the Temple.

short_description.id: The Hairy Leg (perna cabeluda) adalah legenda urban Recife tentang kaki berbulu yang menyerang orang pada malam hari [the-hairy-leg-c01, the-hairy-leg-c03].
short_description.en: The Hairy Leg (perna cabeluda) is a Recife urban legend of a hairy leg that attacks people at night [the-hairy-leg-c01, the-hairy-leg-c03].

long_description.id: The Hairy Leg adalah legenda urban Brasil dari Recife [the-hairy-leg-c01] tentang kaki manusia berbulu yang menjegal dan menendang orang pada malam hari [the-hairy-leg-c03]. Menurut satu sumber, legenda ini diciptakan surat kabar Diário de Pernambuco pada masa kediktatoran militer untuk menggantikan berita yang disensor [the-hairy-leg-c02].
long_description.en: The Hairy Leg is a Brazilian urban legend from Recife [the-hairy-leg-c01] about a hairy human leg that tackles and kicks people at night [the-hairy-leg-c03]. According to one source, the Diário de Pernambuco created it under the military dictatorship to stand in for censored news [the-hairy-leg-c02].

long_description.id: Catatan awalnya dari 10 Desember 1975 [the-hairy-leg-c12]: warga yang diwawancarai menggambarkan kaki yang terpotong, penuh bulu dan kuku, yang menyerang orang pada malam hari [the-hairy-leg-c05], dan kaki itu disebut berukuran sekitar satu setengah meter, berjalan di seluruh rumah, bergantung di atap, dan berubah menjadi hewan [the-hairy-leg-c06]. Dalam tulisan Carrero, untuk pertama kalinya muncul cara kerja yang membuatnya terkenal, yaitu menendang dan menjegal orang [the-hairy-leg-c09].
long_description.en: Its earliest record is from 10 December 1975 [the-hairy-leg-c12]: residents interviewed described a severed leg, full of hair and nails, that attacked people at night [the-hairy-leg-c05], and the leg was said to measure about a metre and a half, walk all over the house, hang from the roof and turn into an animal [the-hairy-leg-c06]. In Carrero's text, the modus operandi that made it famous appears for the first time: kicking and tripping people [the-hairy-leg-c09].

long_description.id: Asal-usul kisah ini tidak jelas dan beberapa jurnalis berbeda mengklaim sebagai penciptanya [the-hairy-leg-c07], termasuk jurnalis Jota Ferreira [the-hairy-leg-c08]. Dalam tahun-tahun berikutnya, Perna Cabeluda menjadi frevo, bloco karnaval, dan kostum [the-hairy-leg-c10]. Menurut Roberto Beltrão, legenda semacam ini di Recife dipakai untuk menyublimasi kepedihan masyarakat [the-hairy-leg-c11]. Film The Secret Agent (2025) menjadikannya unsur utama cerita [the-hairy-leg-c04].
long_description.en: The origins of the story are unclear and several journalists claim authorship [the-hairy-leg-c07], including the journalist Jota Ferreira [the-hairy-leg-c08]. In the following years the Perna Cabeluda became a frevo, a carnival bloco and a costume [the-hairy-leg-c10]. According to Roberto Beltrão, legends like this in Recife were used to sublimate the pains of society [the-hairy-leg-c11]. The film The Secret Agent (2025) made it central to its story [the-hairy-leg-c04].

cultural_context.en: A newspaper invented it to signal material censored by the military regime [the-hairy-leg-c02]; according to Roberto Beltrão, legends like this in Recife were used to sublimate the pains of society [the-hairy-leg-c11].

short_description.id: Morrígan adalah tokoh mitologi Irlandia, dewi perang dan takdir yang meramalkan malapetaka, kematian, atau kemenangan dalam pertempuran, dan sering muncul sebagai burung gagak.
short_description.en: The Morrígan is a figure of Irish mythology, a goddess of war and fate who foretells doom, death or victory in battle and often appears as a crow.

long_description.id: Morrígan atau Mórrígan, juga Morrígu, adalah tokoh dalam mitologi Irlandia (Irish mythology); namanya diterjemahkan sebagai "ratu agung" atau "ratu hantu". Ia terutama dikaitkan dengan perang dan takdir, khususnya meramalkan malapetaka, kematian, atau kemenangan dalam pertempuran, dan dalam peran itu sering muncul sebagai burung gagak, badb. Ia menghasut para pejuang untuk bertempur, membuat musuh ketakutan, dan digambarkan mencuci pakaian berlumur darah milik mereka yang ditakdirkan mati. Ia juga dipandang sebagai wujud dewi bumi dan kedaulatan, penjaga wilayah dan rakyatnya.
long_description.en: The Morrígan or Mórrígan, also Morrígu, is a figure of Irish mythology; her name is rendered "great queen" or "phantom queen". She is chiefly tied to war and fate, above all foretelling doom, death or victory in battle, and in that role often appears as a crow, the badb. She stirs warriors to fight, frightens their foes, and is shown washing the bloodied clothes of those fated to die. She is also seen as a form of the earth and sovereignty goddess, guardian of the land and its people.

long_description.id: Morrígan sering digambarkan sebagai tiga bersaudari, "tiga Morrígna": Badb, Macha, dan Morrígan, yang mungkin bernama Anu, dan diduga semuanya nama bagi dewi yang sama. Ia disebut istri Dagda yang pencemburu dan dewi yang dapat berubah wujud, dan dikaitkan dengan banshee dalam cerita rakyat kemudian. Menurut artikel id, ia dapat menjelma menjadi gadis cantik, pemimpin pasukan, nenek tua, burung gagak, atau burung bangkai; sebagai gagak hitam ia terbang di atas medan perang sambil memekik dan dapat meramalkan hasil pertempuran.
long_description.en: The Morrígan is often shown as three sisters, "the three Morrígna": Badb, Macha and the Morrígan, who may be named Anu, perhaps all names for one goddess. She is called the envious wife of the Dagda and a shape-shifting goddess, and is linked with the banshee of later folklore. According to the id article she can become a beautiful girl, a war leader, an old woman, a crow or a vulture; as a black crow she flies over the battlefield shrieking and can foretell the outcome of the fight.

long_description.id: Arti namanya diperdebatkan: unsur mor mungkin berasal dari akar Indo-Eropa yang bermakna teror, sekerabat dengan maere bahasa Inggris Kuno (yang bertahan dalam kata nightmare), dan rígan berarti "ratu", sehingga tafsiran "Ratu Hantu" kini paling banyak diterima. Sumber tertuanya adalah glos dalam naskah Latin; glosarium O'Mulconry abad ke-8 menyebut Macha salah satu dari tiga morrígna.
long_description.en: The meaning of her name is debated: mor may come from an Indo-European root meaning terror, akin to Old English maere (surviving in nightmare), and rígan means "queen", so "Phantom Queen" is now the most favoured reading. The earliest sources are glosses in Latin manuscripts; the 8th-century O'Mulconry's Glossary names Macha as one of the three morrígna.

claims.quote: The Morrígan or Mórrígan, also known as Morrígu, is a figure from Irish mythology. The name is Mór-ríoghan in modern Irish before the spelling reform, and it has been translated as "great queen" or "phantom queen". The Morrígan is mainly associated with war and fate, especially with foretelling doom, death, or victory in battle. In this role she often appears as a crow, the badb.

statement.id: Morrígan (Mórrígan, Morrígu, Mór-ríoghan) adalah tokoh mitologi Irlandia (Irish mythology), "ratu agung" atau "ratu hantu", terkait perang dan takdir, meramalkan malapetaka, kematian, atau kemenangan, sering sebagai gagak (crow), badb.
statement.en: The Morrígan (Mórrígan, Morrígu, Mór-ríoghan) is a figure of Irish mythology, "great queen" or "phantom queen", tied to war and fate, foretelling doom, death or victory, often as a crow, the badb.

claims.quote: The Morrígan encourages warriors to do brave deeds, strikes fear into their enemies, and is portrayed washing the bloodstained clothes of those fated to die.

statement.id: Morrígan mendorong pejuang berani, menakuti musuh, dan mencuci pakaian berlumur darah milik yang ditakdirkan mati.
statement.en: The Morrígan spurs warriors to brave deeds, frightens their foes and washes the bloodstained clothes of those fated to die.

claims.quote: She is most frequently seen as a goddess of battle and war and has also been seen as a manifestation of the earth- and sovereignty-goddess, chiefly representing the goddess's role as guardian of the territory and its people.

statement.id: Ia dipandang sebagai dewi pertempuran dan perang, juga wujud dewi bumi dan kedaulatan, penjaga wilayah dan rakyat.
statement.en: She is seen as a goddess of battle and war, and as a form of the earth and sovereignty goddess, guardian of land and people.

claims.quote: The Morrígan is often described as a trio of individuals, all sisters, called "the three Morrígna". In mythology membership of the triad is given as Badb, Macha, and the Morrigan, who may be named Anu. It is believed that these were all names for the same goddess.

statement.id: Morrígan sering digambarkan sebagai tiga bersaudari (three Morrígna): Badb, Macha, dan Morrigan yang mungkin bernama Anu, mungkin nama dewi yang sama.
statement.en: The Morrígan is often three sisters, the three Morrígna: Badb, Macha and the Morrigan, who may be named Anu, perhaps names of one goddess.

claims.quote: The Morrígan is described as the envious wife of The Dagda and a shape-shifting goddess

statement.id: Morrígan digambarkan sebagai istri Dagda (The Dagda) yang pencemburu dan dewi yang berubah wujud.
statement.en: The Morrígan is described as the envious wife of The Dagda and a shape-shifting goddess.

claims.quote: She is associated with the banshee of later folklore.

statement.id: Ia dikaitkan dengan banshee dalam cerita rakyat kemudian.
statement.en: She is associated with the banshee of later folklore.

claims.quote: Ia dapat mengubah wujudnya menjadi seorang gadis rupawan, pemimpin pasukan, nenek tua, dan burung gagak maupun burung bangkai (hering).

statement.id: Morrigan dapat menjelma gadis rupawan, pemimpin pasukan, nenek tua, burung gagak, atau burung bangkai (hering).
statement.en: The Morrigan can become a fair maiden, war leader, old woman, crow or vulture (burung bangkai).

claims.quote: Citra gagak hitam sering muncul dalam suatu peperangan yang mana ia terbang diatas medan perang sambil mengeluarkan lengkingannya dan mampu meramalkan hasil peperangan tersebut.

statement.id: Sebagai gagak hitam ia terbang di atas medan perang sambil melengking dan meramalkan hasil peperangan.
statement.en: As a black crow (gagak hitam) she flies over the battlefield (medan perang) shrieking and foretells the outcome (hasil peperangan).

claims.quote: Mor may derive from an Indo-European root connoting terror, monstrousness, cognate with the Old English maere (which survives in the modern English word "nightmare") and the Scandinavian mara

statement.id: Unsur Mor mungkin dari akar Indo-Eropa (Indo-European) bermakna teror, sekerabat dengan maere (Old English, Inggris Kuno) dalam kata nightmare dan mara Skandinavia (Scandinavian).
statement.en: Mor may come from an Indo-European root of terror, akin to Old English maere (in nightmare) and Scandinavian mara.

claims.quote: The earliest sources for the Morrígan are glosses in Latin manuscripts and glossaries (collections of glosses). The 8th century O'Mulconry's Glossary says that Macha is one of the three morrígna.

statement.id: Sumber tertua adalah glos dalam naskah Latin (Latin); O'Mulconry's Glossary abad ke-8 menyebut Macha salah satu tiga morrígna.
statement.en: The earliest sources are glosses in Latin manuscripts; the 8th-century O'Mulconry's Glossary names Macha one of the three morrígna.

claims.quote: while rígan translates as "queen". This etymological sequence can be reconstructed in the Proto-Celtic language as *Moro-rīganī-s. Accordingly, Morrígan is often translated as "Phantom Queen". This is the derivation generally favoured in current scholarship.

statement.id: Rígan berarti ratu (queen); Morrígan diartikan Ratu Hantu (Phantom Queen), tafsiran yang paling diterima kini.
statement.en: Rígan means queen; Morrígan is read as Phantom Queen, the derivation now favoured.

selection_criteria: computeFillStatus must be lengkap-informasi: complete, valid research without an approved image.
No active editorial artwork and no permanent artwork exclusion.
The accepted research entry is embedded unchanged; the image may only depict what its claims document.
Creatures an earlier batch left out keep that reason as catatan_sebelumnya; the generator may decline them with status tidak-digambar.

user_policy.name: sangar
user_policy.intent: Every illustration must feel 'sangar': dangerous, imposing or awe-inspiring, with the being as the undeniable subject. The owner rejected earlier images that read as an ordinary person, an ordinary animal, an empty landscape, or a calm, cute or decorative portrait. Those outcomes are failures regardless of technical quality.
user_policy.subject: The being dominates the frame and is clearly the subject. Head, eyes and distinguishing traits are readable even at thumbnail size. Never a landscape without the being, never a human who could be a passer-by, never a farm animal at pasture.
user_policy.moment: Depict a moment, not a pose: hunting, emerging, striking, commanding, towering, descending, tearing through weather or ground. Gaze and posture confront or loom over the viewer. Standing still and facing the camera with a neutral expression is not acceptable.
user_policy.effects: Visible power is wanted and may be strong, but every effect must come from a power, domain, attribute, habitat or deed documented in the research claims of that being, and it must act physically on the world: ground cracking, water rearing, trees bending, lightning striking, flame consuming, fog pouring, bodies of victims turned to stone. No generic glowing envelope, neon outline, energy ribbons, floating runes or luminous coloured mist. If the research documents no power, build menace from anatomy, scale, moment, light and setting instead, and record that in artistic_choices.
user_policy.fidelity: Anatomy, attributes, number of heads, eyes, limbs and iconography follow the research claims exactly. Effects and atmosphere add power; they never replace or invent anatomy. Fully opaque clothing where a humanlike form is clothed; no nudity, no explicit gore.
user_policy.composition: Low camera angle; monumental or predatory scale with small environmental references when size is documented, otherwise dominance through tight framing and foreshortening. Strong silhouette, high contrast, cinematic low-key lighting from one dominant source (moon, fire, lightning, dying sun), rim light, dust, smoke, rain or spray. Tactile surfaces: wet scales, matted fur, cracked skin, rust, weathered cloth, stone.
user_policy.setting: The place its stories name: graveyard, swamp, sea cliff, battlefield, celestial palace, desert storm. Weather and time of day heighten threat or majesty. Palette is dark and warm with one strong accent, consistent with the collection; no pastel, no flat even daylight.
user_policy.respect: Living religions (Hindu, Buddhist, Shinto, Abrahamic and folk deities still worshipped) are majestic and overwhelming rather than monstrous: cosmic scale, divine radiance from documented attributes, the elements they rule in motion. Malevolent beings are menacing. Literary beings follow their source text, never a film, game, anime or comic design.
user_policy.aniconic: If the research documents no bodily form at all, either depict the documented manifestation as an active, overwhelming force (the sky itself splitting, a storm swallowing the steppe) with the choice recorded in artistic_choices, or decline the entry with status tidak-digambar. A calm scene without agency fails.
user_policy.self_check: Before accepting an image the generator answers all of these with yes: the being dominates the frame; it still looks dangerous or majestic at 200 px; there is a moment, not a static pose; each visible effect points to a claim id; head, eye and limb counts match the claims; no text, watermark, border or borrowed design; it would not be rejected as ordinary person, ordinary animal, landscape only, or cute and calm. One no means regenerate, keep the rejected attempt as history, up to three attempts.
user_policy.style: Square premium painterly cinematic illustration in the house style of the existing artwork, more dramatic and higher contrast. No text, labels, logo, border or watermark.
user_policy.sources: Never copy designs from films, games, anime or comics (modern_depictions). Every design is original and sourced from the accepted research.
